Document: Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot
Part 3 of 10
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (5A) On receipt of the claimant’s online directions questionnaire–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (a) the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined) for 28 days, to allow for mediation, and the 28-day period is calculated from and including the date that the response from the claimant is received by the court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (b) the court must also refer the matter to the Small Claims Mediation Service and tell the parties that the matter has been referred. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (8) The claimant must tell the court if a settlement is reached. The claimant must also tell the court if the parties have agreed that the claim can be discontinued by sending form N279 Notice of Discontinuance to the “CNBC” (as defined). If the claimant discontinues the claim the court must send the claim form out of the pilot to the “CNBC” (as defined) for the claim to proceed as if it had been started under CPR Part 7. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (Section 10A contains provisions about informing the court of settlement and discontinuance.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (9) If the 28 day stay of proceedings ends without the claimant telling the court that a settlement has been reached –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (a) a legal adviser may consider the forms under Section 20, Table A if the “preferred court” (as defined) is one of the county court hearing centres in relation to which Online Civil Money Claims legal advisers operate; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (b) a judge may consider the forms. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (9A) If the forms are not considered by a judge or legal adviser under subparagraph (9), the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined), and the court must tell the parties that the claim has been sent out, and explain why. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (10) If a settlement is reached within the 28 days, but the parties have not agreed that the claim can be dismissed or discontinued, the court must stay the proceedings. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (11) If the court receives a further application in relation to the settlement agreement, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined). The court must inform the claimant and defendant that the claim has been sent out of Online Civil Money Claims, and explain why the claim has been sent out. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (12) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (13) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (14) Once the claim has been sent out of Online Civil Money Claims, this practice direction will no longer apply, but the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will continue to apply with the following changes –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (i) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (ii) Civil Procedure Rules 26.4, 26.5 and 26.6 do not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (iii) if an “order for allocation” has been made while the claim is in Online Civil Money Claims, Civil Procedure Rules 26.7 does not apply. (An “order for allocation” is a court order that sets out what route (known as a “track”) the case will follow, based on the value of the claim and how complicated the case is.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (On a claim being sent out, any party’s online directions questionnaire is treated as their completed directions questionnaire form N180 – see paragraph 19.1(5). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] Sub-section C – defendant defending the claim: the claim amount exceeds £10,000 excluding interest

## 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (2) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept the defendant’s defence, or whether they do not accept it and wish to continue with the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (3) If, within 33 days after being asked by the court, the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they do not wish to continue with the claim, the claim will be automatically “stayed” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (4) If the claimant fails to respond online within the 33 days, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (5) If, within 33 days after being asked by the court, the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they wish to continue with the claim, then at the same time, the claimant must also submit their completed online directions questionnaire to the court, to tell the court what requirements the claimant would have, should a court hearing be necessary, including, if the claim appears suitable for the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track, proposed  directions. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (6) Once the court has received the claimant’s online directions questionnaire and if the amount of the claim excluding interest is £25,000 or less–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (a) a legal adviser may consider the forms under Section 20, Table A if the amount claimed is £10,000 or less and the “preferred court” (as defined) is one of the county court hearing centres in relation to which Online Civil Money Claims legal advisers operate; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (b) a judge may consider the forms. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (7) If the forms are not considered by a judge or legal adviser under subparagraph (6) or the amount of the claim excluding interest exceeds £25,000, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined), and the court must tell the parties that the claim has been sent out, and explain why. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (8) Once the claim has been sent out of Online Civil Money Claims, this practice direction will no longer apply, but the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will continue to apply with the following changes –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (a) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (b) Civil Procedure Rules 26.4, 26.5 and 26.6 do not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (c) if an “order for allocation” has been made while the claim is in Online Civil Money Claims, Civil Procedure Rules 26.7 does not apply. (An “order for allocation” is a court order that sets out what route (known as a “track”) the case will follow, based on the value of the claim and how complicated the case is.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.3(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section C of Section 6 applies.] (On a claim being sent out, any party’s online directions questionnaire is treated as their completed directions questionnaire form N180 – see paragraph 19.1(5)). ## 6.4 Omitted

## 6.5 Omitted

## 6.6 Omitted

## 6.7 Omitted

## 6.8 Omitted

## SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] Application of this Section

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] 6A.1(1) This Section applies where at least one of the parties is represented by a legal representative. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (2) This Section is subject to paragraph 7.48 (multi-party claims over £25,000 excluding interest where defendants’ responses differ). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] Defendant’s response to the claim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] 6A.2 (1) Unless the parties have agreed a time extension under subparagraph (2), the defendant must respond to the claim by completing and submitting the response form to the court using the OCMC website by 4pm on the 28 th day after the issue of the claim form. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (2)  The parties may agree an extension of time of up to 28 days in total. The defendant must record on the OCMC website any such agreed extension of time before the expiry of the original 28 day time limit. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (3) If a time extension has been agreed and recorded under subparagraph (2), the defendant must respond to the claim using the OCMC website by 4pm on the last day of the agreed extended time. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (4)  If the parties have agreed an extension of time of less than 28 days but then wish to increase the extension up to 28 days in total, the defendant must make an application. (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] Defendant’s response – defence and counterclaim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] 6A.3 If the defendant responds to defend the claim and make a counterclaim, the court must send the claim out of the pilot to the CNBC for the claim to continue as if it had started under CPR Part 7. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] Defendant’s response – defend the whole of the claim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] 6A.4 (1) If the defendant responds to defend the whole of the claim, at the same time that they submit their response form, they must submit the directions questionnaire, by completing and submitting the relevant screens using the OCMC website, including, if the claim  appears suitable for the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track, proposed directions. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (2) The defendant’s response must include the information required by CPR 16.5. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (3) If the defendant responds to the claim with a defence, the claimant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (a)  indicate whether they want to continue with the claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (b) if they do want to continue with the claim, complete the directions questionnaire using the OCMC website,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] before 4pm on the 28th day after date of notification of the defendant’s response. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (4) If, before the expiry of the time limit in subparagraph (3), the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they do not wish to continue with the claim, the claim will be automatically “stayed” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (5) Subject to subparagraph (6), if the claimant does not comply with subparagraph (3) within the time specified in that subparagraph—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (a) the claim will, at that point, be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims to a County Court Hearing Centre under paragraph 19.1;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (b) the claim will be treated in the same way as if the claimant had failed to comply with a notice served under CPR 26.4(1); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (c) an order will be made under CPR 26.4(9). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (6) In a claim where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (a) the claimant does not comply with subparagraph (3) within the time specified in that subparagraph; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] (b) the defendant is represented by a legal representative but the claimant is not,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6A – AT LEAST ONE PARTY IS REPRESENTED – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE TO THE CLAIM] Defendant’s response –defend the whole of the claim: claim not exceeding £10,000 excluding interest

## 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) the defendant is defending the whole of the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) the claim is a claim for a specified amount of money only not exceeding £10,000 excluding interest; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (2) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (3) If the claimant has not opted out of mediation –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined) for 28 days, to allow for mediation, and the 28-day period is calculated from and including the date that the response from the claimant is received by the court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) the court must also refer the matter to the Small Claims Mediation Service and tell the parties that the matter has been referred. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (4) The claimant must tell the court if a settlement is reached. The claimant must also tell the court if the parties have agreed that the claim can be discontinued or dismissed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (Section 10A contains provisions about informing the court of settlement and discontinuance.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (5) If the 28 day stay of proceedings ends without the claimant telling the court that a settlement has been reached –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) a legal adviser may consider the forms under Section 20, Table A the “preferred court” (as defined) is one of the county court hearing centres in relation to which Online Civil Money Claims legal advisers operate; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) a judge may consider the forms. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (6) If the forms are not considered by a judge or legal adviser under subparagraph (5), the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined), and the court must tell the parties that the claim has been sent out, and explain why. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (7) If a settlement is reached within the 28 days, but the parties have not agreed that the claim can be dismissed or discontinued, the court must stay the proceedings. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (8) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (9) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (10) Once the claim has been sent out of Online Civil Money Claims, this practice direction will no longer apply, but the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will continue to apply with the following changes –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) Civil Procedure Rules 26.4, 26.5, 26.6 do not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) if an “order for allocation” has been made while the claim is in Online Civil Money Claims, Civil Procedure Rule 26.7 does not apply. (An “order for allocation” is a court order that sets out what route (known as a “track”) the case will follow, based on the value of the claim and how complicated the case is.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] (On a claim being sent out, any party’s online directions questionnaire is treated as their completed directions questionnaire form N180 – see paragraph 19.1(5)). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.5(1) This paragraph applies if –] Defendant’s response – defend the whole of the claim and claim exceeds £10,000

## 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) the defendant is defending the whole of the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) the claim is –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (i) a claim for a specified amount of money only exceeding £10,000 excluding interest; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (A2) Sub-paragraph (2) applies if –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) the amount of the claim excluding interest is £25,000 or less; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) the amount of the claim excluding interest is £25,000 or more and –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (i) all the parties are legally represented; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (ii) where there is more than one defendant, both defendants have responded to defend the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (2) Where this sub-paragraph  applies, once the court has received the claimant’s directions questionnaire –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) a legal adviser may consider the forms under Section 20, Table A if the amount claimed is £10,000 or less and the “preferred court” (as defined) is one of the county court hearing centres in relation to which Online Civil Money Claims legal advisers operate; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) a judge may consider the forms. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (3) If the forms are not considered by a judge or legal adviser under subparagraph (2), or if sub-paragraph (2) does not apply, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “preferred court” (as defined), and the court must tell the parties that the claim has been sent out, and explain why. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (4) Once the claim has been sent out of Online Civil Money Claims, this practice direction will no longer apply, but the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will continue to apply with the following changes –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (a) Civil Procedure Rules 26.4, 26.5, 26.6 do not apply; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (b) if an “order for allocation” has been made while the claim is in Online Civil Money Claims, Civil Procedure Rule 26.7 does not apply. (An “order for allocation” is a court order that sets out what route (known as a “track”) the case will follow, based on the value of the claim and how complicated the case is.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6A.6(1) This paragraph applies if –] (On a claim being sent out, any party’s directions questionnaire is treated as their completed directions questionnaire form N180 – see paragraph 19.1(5)). ## SECTION 6B – OMITTED

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] Following first case management directions, defended claims to be sent out in certain circumstances

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] 6C.1 Once a judge or legal adviser has considered the forms under paragraphs 6A.5(5) or 6A.6(2) and made directions, the claim is to be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims unless–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (a) all the parties are represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (b) at least one party is represented and–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (i) no party has completed a screen in Welsh; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (ii) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (iii) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (iv) the claim has not been allocated to the intermediate track or multi-track; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (c) neither party is represented by a legal representative and –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (i) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (ii) neither party has completed a screen in Welsh; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (iii) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (iv) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (v) the claim has not be allocated to the intermediate track or multi-track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] (If the claim is not sent out and the claim is proceeding in a County Court hearing centre other than in Birmingham, the claim remains in Online Civil Money Claims so that this practice direction continues to apply.). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] Filing and exchanging of budgets

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] 6C.2 In those claims to which the provisions of Section II of Civil Procedure Rules Part 3 and Practice Direction 3D apply, CPR 3.13(1)(a) is disapplied and all parties except litigants in person must file and exchange budgets in accordance with Civil Procedure Rule 3.13(1)(b), namely not later than 21 days before the first case management conference. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 6B – OMITTED] Claims allocated to the fast track –Trial readiness certificate

## 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (2) Civil Procedure Rule 28.4 and 28.5 do not apply, except to the extent provided for by subparagraph (6). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6C.3(1 ) This paragraph applies where a claim is allocated to the fast track.] (3) Within 2 weeks of notice from the court via the OCMC website to do so, the parties must use the relevant screens on the OCMC website to complete and submit a “trial readiness certificate”, to indicate whether they are ready for trial and to update any hearing requirements already given to the court.
